text: For a reaction, $\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{5(\mathrm{g})}\to 2\mathrm{NO}_{2(\mathrm{g})}+\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{g})}$ in a constant volume container, no products were present initially. The final pressure of the system when $50%$ of reaction gets completed is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At constant volume and temperature, partial pressure is proportional to moles. With initial pressure $P_{0}$ of $\mathrm{N}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{5}$ and a decrease $x$ in its pressure:

$\mathrm{N}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{5}(\mathrm{g})\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$

$p_{\mathrm{N}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{5}}=P_{0}-x,p_{\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}}=2x,p_{\mathrm{O}{}_{2}}=\dfrac{x}{2}$

$P_{\text{total}}=(P_{0}-x)+2x+\dfrac{x}{2}=P_{0}+\dfrac{3x}{2}$

At $50%$ completion, $x=\dfrac{P_{0}}{2}$:

$P_{\text{total}}=P_{0}+\dfrac{3}{2}\times \dfrac{P_{0}}{2}=\dfrac{7}{4}P_{0}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text: Consider the given plots of vapour pressure (VP) vs temperature(T/K). Which amongst the following options is correct graphical representation showing $\Delta \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{f}}$, depression in the freezing point of a solvent in a solution?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The freezing point of a liquid is the temperature at which its vapour pressure equals that of the solid, i.e. where its vapour-pressure curve meets the steep vapour-pressure curve of the frozen solvent. Only pure solvent freezes out, so the same solid curve applies to the solvent and to the solution.

A non-volatile solute lowers the vapour pressure, so the solution curve lies below the liquid-solvent curve at every temperature and meets the solid curve at a lower temperature: $T_{f}<T_{f}^{\circ }$ and $\Delta T_{f}=T_{f}^{\circ }-T_{f}$.

Figure (C) shows exactly this. In (B) the solution curve lies above the liquid solvent, and (A) and (D) mark where two curves reach a fixed vapour pressure, which is the boiling-point construction.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

solution.body:
Hydration of propyne with $\mathrm{Hg}{}^{2+}/\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$ follows Markovnikov's rule, and the enol tautomerises to propanone:

$\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}-\mathrm{C}\equiv \mathrm{CH}{}^{\mathrm{Hg}{}^{2+},\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$

$\mathrm{HCN}$ adds to the carbonyl group, giving the cyanohydrin $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})\mathrm{CN}$.

$\mathrm{H}{}_{2}/\mathrm{Ni}$ reduces $-\mathrm{C}\equiv \mathrm{N}$ to $-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$, giving $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$ (1-amino-2-methylpropan-2-ol), in which $\mathrm{OH}$ and $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ sit on the same carbon.

Option (A) would need propanal, which Markovnikov hydration of propyne does not give.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{sp}}$ for $\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{OH})_{3}$ is $1.6\times 10^{-30}$. What is the molar solubility of this salt in water?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the molar solubility of $\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{OH})_{3}$ in water, we start with the dissolution equilibrium:

$\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{OH})_{3(\mathrm{s})}⇌\mathrm{Cr}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{3+}_{s}+3\mathrm{OH}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{-}_{3s}$

At equilibrium, the solubility product $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{sp}}$ is given by:

$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{sp}}=(\mathrm{s})\cdot (3\mathrm{s})^{3}=27\mathrm{s}^{4}$

Substituting the given $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{sp}}$ value:

$27\mathrm{s}^{4}=1.6\times 10^{-30}$

Solving for $\mathrm{s}$, we divide both sides by 27:

$\mathrm{s}=\left (\frac{1.6\times 10^{-30}}{27}\right )^{1/4}$

Thus, the molar solubility of $\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{OH})_{3}$ is:

$\left (\frac{1.6}{27}\times 10^{-30}\right )^{1/4}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text:
Which of the following linear combination of atomic orbitals will lead to formation of molecular orbitals in homonuclear diatomic molecules [internuclear axis in $z$-direction] ?

A. $2\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{z}}$ and $2\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{x}}$

B. 2 s and $2\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{x}}$

C. $3d_{xy}$ and $3d_{x^{2}-y^{2}}$

D. 2 s and $2\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{z}}$

E. $2p_{z}$ and $3d_{x^{2}-y^{2}}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A molecular orbital forms only when the two atomic orbitals have the same symmetry about the internuclear ($z$) axis, so that their net overlap is non-zero.

$2s$ and $2p_{z}$ are both cylindrically symmetric about the $z$-axis ($σ$ type), so they overlap along the axis and form $σ$ molecular orbitals: D is valid.

$2p_{x}$ is of $π$ type about the $z$-axis; its lobes of opposite sign overlap equally with $2p_{z}$ (A) or with $2s$ (B), so the net overlap is zero.

$3d_{xy}$ and $3d_{x^{2}-y^{2}}$ are both $δ$ type about the $z$-axis, but $3d_{xy}$ changes sign on reflection through the $xz$-plane while $3d_{x^{2}-y^{2}}$ does not, so their net overlap is zero (C).

$2p_{z}$ ($σ$ type) and $3d_{x^{2}-y^{2}}$ ($δ$ type) differ in symmetry about the axis, so their net overlap is zero (E).

Only combination D leads to molecular orbitals.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text:
Which of the following statements are NOT true about the periodic table?

A. The properties of elements are function of atomic weights.

B. The properties of elements are function of atomic numbers.

C. Elements having similar outer electronic configurations are arranged in same period.

D. An element's location reflects the quantum numbers of the last filled orbital.

E. The number of elements in a period is same as the number of atomic orbitals available in energy level that is being filled.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
By the modern periodic law, the properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers, not atomic weights: A is not true and B is true.

Elements with similar outer electronic configurations are placed in the same group (vertical column), not in the same period: C is not true.

The period of an element gives the principal quantum number of its outermost shell and its block gives the subshell receiving the last electron, so its location reflects the quantum numbers of the last orbital filled: D is true.

The number of elements in a period is twice the number of atomic orbitals available in the energy level being filled; for example, period 2 fills the 2s and 2p orbitals (4 orbitals) and has 8 elements: E is not true.

The statements that are NOT true are A, C and E.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text: One mole of the octahedral complex compound $\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}\mathrm{Cl}_{3}$ gives 3 moles of ions on dissolution in water. One mole of the same complex reacts with excess of $\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}$ solution to yield two moles of $\mathrm{AgCl}_{(\mathrm{s})}$. The structure of the complex is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
An octahedral Co(III) complex holds six ligands in the coordination sphere; only chloride outside the sphere ionises and precipitates as AgCl.

3 mol of ions per mole means one complex ion and two counter ions, and 2 mol of AgCl means two ionisable $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$, so the sphere holds five $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ and one Cl.

$[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{5}\mathrm{Cl}]\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}\longrightarrow [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{5}\mathrm{Cl}]{}^{2+}+2\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$

$[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{5}\mathrm{Cl}]\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}+2\mathrm{AgNO}{}_{3}\longrightarrow [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{5}\mathrm{Cl}](\mathrm{NO}{}_{3}){}_{2}+2\mathrm{AgCl}$

In (B) the sphere has only five ligands, (C) is a non-electrolyte giving no AgCl, and (D) gives 2 ions and 1 mol AgCl.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text:
Which of the following statement is true with respect to $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O},\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ and $\mathrm{CH}_{4}$ ?

A. The central atoms of all the molecules are $\mathrm{sp}^{3}$ hybridized.

B. The $\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H},\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{H}$ and $\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}$ angles in the above molecules are $104.5^{\circ },107.5^{\circ }$ and $109.5^{\circ }$, respectively.

C. The increasing order of dipole moment is $\mathrm{CH}_{4}<\mathrm{NH}_{3}<\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$.

D. Both $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ and $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ are Lewis acids and $\mathrm{CH}_{4}$ is a Lewis base.

E. A solution of $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ in $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ is basic. In this solution $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ and $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ act as Lowry-Bronsted acid and base respectively.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, C and E Only
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$, $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ and $\mathrm{CH}{}_{4}$ the central atom has four electron pairs (2 bp + 2 lp, 3 bp + 1 lp and 4 bp + 0 lp), so all three are $sp^{3}$ hybridised. A is true.

Lone pair–bond pair repulsion closes the angle below the tetrahedral value: $109.5^{\circ }$ in $\mathrm{CH}{}_{4}$, about $107.5^{\circ }$ in $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ (one lone pair) and $104.5^{\circ }$ in $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ (two lone pairs). B is true.

$\mathrm{CH}{}_{4}$ is symmetric and non-polar (0 D), and $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ (1.47 D) is less polar than $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ (1.85 D), so $\mathrm{CH}{}_{4}<\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}<\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ is correct. C is true.

$\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ and $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ donate lone pairs, so both are Lewis bases, while $\mathrm{CH}{}_{4}$ has neither a lone pair nor a vacant orbital and is not a Lewis base. D is false.

In $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}\qquad +\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}{}^{+}+\mathrm{OH}{}^{-}$, $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ accepts a proton (Brønsted base) and $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ donates it (Brønsted acid), the reverse of what E states. E is false.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text: Let us consider an endothermic reaction which is non-spontaneous at the freezing point of water. However, the reaction is spontaneous at boiling point of water. Choose the correct option.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A reaction is spontaneous when $\Delta G=\Delta H-T\Delta S<0$.

The reaction is endothermic, so $\Delta H>0$. If $\Delta S$ were negative, both $\Delta H$ and $-T\Delta S$ would be positive and $\Delta G$ would be positive at every temperature.

With $\Delta H>0$ and $\Delta S>0$, $\Delta G>0$ at low temperature and $\Delta G<0$ once $T>\dfrac{\Delta H}{\Delta S}$, so the reaction is non-spontaneous at 273 K and spontaneous at 373 K.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text: Which of the following arrangements with respect to their reactivity in nucleophilic addition reaction is correct?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Nucleophilic addition to a carbonyl group is slowed by groups that crowd the carbonyl carbon or reduce its positive charge, and speeded up by electron-withdrawing groups that increase its electrophilicity.

Acetophenone is a ketone: its methyl group adds steric hindrance and $+I$ donation, so it is the least reactive.

Among the aldehydes, the $p$-$\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ group of $p$-tolualdehyde donates electrons ($+I$, hyperconjugation) and makes the carbonyl carbon less electrophilic than in benzaldehyde, while the $p$-$\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ group ($-I$, $-R$) makes it more electrophilic.

$\text{acetophenone}<p\text{-tolualdehyde}<\text{benzaldehyde}<p\text{-nitrobenzaldehyde}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text:
The carbohydrate "Ribose" present in DNA, is

A. A pentose sugar

B. present in pyranose form

C. in "D" configuration

D. a reducing sugar, when free

E. in $α$-anomeric form

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The sugar of DNA is 2-deoxy-D-ribose, present in the nucleotides as the five-membered ring $β$-furanose, $β$-2-deoxy-D-ribofuranose:


[IMG]

A: it has five carbon atoms, so it is a pentose. Correct.

B: the ring contains four carbons and one oxygen (furanose), not five carbons and one oxygen (pyranose). Incorrect.

C: the $\mathrm{OH}$ on C-4, the stereocentre farthest from the aldehyde carbon, lies on the right in the Fischer projection, so it is a D-sugar. Correct.

D: when free, the ring opens to a free $\mathrm{CHO}$ group, which reduces Tollens' and Fehling's reagents, so it is a reducing sugar. Correct.

E: in DNA the base is joined to C-1 by a $β$-glycosidic link, so the sugar is in the $β$-anomeric form, not $α$. Incorrect.

So statements A, C and D are correct.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text:
$37.8\mathrm{g}\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{5}$ was taken in a 1 L reaction vessel and allowed to undergo the following reaction at 500 K

$2\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{5(\mathrm{g})}⇌2\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4(\mathrm{g})}+\mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{g})}$

The total pressure at equilibrium was found to be 18.65 bar.

Then, $\mathrm{Kp}=$ $_________$ $\times 10^{-2}$ [nearest integer]

Assume $\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{5}$ to behave ideally under these conditions.

Given: $\mathrm{R}=0.082$ bar $\mathrm{L}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}\mathrm{K}^{-1}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \text{Initial pressure of}\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{5} \\  \\ =\dfrac{\frac{37.8}{108}\times 0.082\times 500}{1}=14.35\mathrm{bar} \\ 2\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{5}⇌2\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}+\mathrm{O}_{2} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{t}=0 14.35 \\ \mathrm{t}=\mathrm{eq}14.35-2\mathrm{P}2\mathrm{P}\mathrm{P} \\ \mathrm{P}_{\text{Total}}\text{at eqb}=14.35+\mathrm{P}=18.65 \\ \mathrm{P}=4.3 \\ \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{5}}=5.75\mathrm{bar} \\ \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}}=8.6\mathrm{bar} \\ \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{O}_{2}}=4.3\mathrm{bar} \\ \mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{p}}=\dfrac{(8.6)^{2}\times (4.3)}{(5.75)^{2}}=9.619=\mathrm{x}\times 10^{-2} \\ \mathrm{x}=961.9\approx 962 \end{array}$

Consider the following reaction occurring in the blast furnace:

$\mathrm{Fe}_{3}\mathrm{O}_{4(\mathrm{s})}+4\mathrm{CO}_{(\mathrm{g})}\to 3\mathrm{Fe}_{(\mathrm{l})}+4\mathrm{CO}_{2(\mathrm{g})}$

' $x$ ' kg of iron is produced when $2.32\times 10^{3}\mathrm{kg}\mathrm{Fe}_{3}\mathrm{O}_{4}$ and $2.8\times 10^{2}\mathrm{kg}\mathrm{CO}$ are brought together in the furnace. The value of ' $x$ ' is $_________ . ($nearest integer)

{Given:
molar mass of $\mathrm{Fe}_{3}\mathrm{O}_{4}=232\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

molar mass of $\mathrm{CO}=28\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

molar mass of $\mathrm{Fe}=56\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$}
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
moles of $\mathrm{Fe}_{3}\mathrm{O}_{4}=\frac{2.32\times 10^{3}\times 10^{3}}{232}=10000\mathrm{mol}$

moles of $\mathrm{CO}=\frac{2.8\times 10^{2}\times 10^{3}}{28}=10000\mathrm{mol}$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{Fe}_{3}\mathrm{O}_{4}+4\mathrm{CO}⟶3\mathrm{Fe}+4\mathrm{CO}_{2} \\ 10^{4}\mathrm{mol}10^{4}\mathrm{mol} \end{array}$

CO is L.R.

mole of $\mathrm{Fe}=\frac{3}{4}\times 10^{4}$

mass of $\mathrm{Fe}=\frac{3}{4}\times \frac{10^{4}\times 56}{1000}\mathrm{kg}=420\mathrm{kg}$

Xg of benzoic acid on reaction with aq $\mathrm{NaHCO}_{3}$ released $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ that occupied 11.2 L volume at STP.

X is $_________ g$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{5}\mathrm{COOH}+\mathrm{NaHCO}_{3}\to \mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{5}\mathrm{COO}^{-}\mathrm{Na}^{+} \\ +\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}+\mathrm{CO}_{2} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{x}\mathrm{gm}\text{11.2 L} \\ \text{mole of}\mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{5}\mathrm{COOH}=\text{mole of}\mathrm{CO}_{2}=\dfrac{11.2}{22.4}=0.5 \\ \text{mass of}\mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{5}\mathrm{COOH}=\mathrm{x}=0.5\times 122=61\mathrm{gm} \end{array}$

text:
Standard entropies of $\mathrm{X}_{2},\mathrm{Y}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{XY}_{5}$ are 70, 50 and $110\mathrm{J}\mathrm{K}^{-1}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ respectively. The temperature in Kelvin at which the reaction

$\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{X}_{2}+\frac{5}{2}\mathrm{Y}_{2}⇌\mathrm{XY}_{5}\Delta \mathrm{H}^{⊖}=-35\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

will be at equilibrium is $__________ ($Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the temperature at which the given reaction is at equilibrium, we need to apply the concept of Gibbs free energy change $(\Delta G^{0})$ at equilibrium, where $\Delta G^{0}$ is equal to zero. 

The given reaction is:

$\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{X}_{2}+\frac{5}{2}\mathrm{Y}_{2}⇌\mathrm{XY}_{5}$

We are given the standard entropies and enthalpy change ($\Delta H^{⊖}$):

Standard entropies: 

$\mathrm{X}_{2}=70\mathrm{J}\mathrm{K}^{-1}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

$\mathrm{Y}_{2}=50\mathrm{J}\mathrm{K}^{-1}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

$\mathrm{XY}_{5}=110\mathrm{J}\mathrm{K}^{-1}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

Standard enthalpy change: 

$\Delta H^{⊖}=-35\mathrm{kJ}/\mathrm{mol}$

First, calculate the standard entropy change ($\Delta S_{Rxn}^{0}$) of the reaction:

$\Delta S_{Rxn}^{0}=110-\left (\frac{1}{2}\times 70+\frac{5}{2}\times 50\right )$

$=110-(35+125)$

$=110-160$

$=-50\mathrm{J}\mathrm{K}^{-1}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

At equilibrium, $\Delta G^{0}=0$, and the relation $\Delta G^{0}=\Delta H^{0}-T\Delta S^{0}$ applies. Thus:

$0=-35000\mathrm{J}/\mathrm{mol}-T(-50\mathrm{J}\mathrm{K}^{-1}\mathrm{mol}^{-1})$

Solving for $T$:

$T\cdot 50=35000$

$T=\frac{35000}{50}$

$T=700\mathrm{K}$

Therefore, the temperature at which the reaction is at equilibrium is 700 Kelvin.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift
